scope: Assemble the accepted demand controller and accepted paid route policy into one bounded autonomous controller that forms its own route-free request, chooses and pays a lawful route, performs actual native content work, creates and pays the deterministic same-scope consumer, and settles the originating demand. This sub-batch stops before honest closure and retained-capability reuse; FT4.3b retains those parent obligations and the common FT4 gate.
rules: The public step interface accepts the engine, actor, historical state, a same-scope FT3 Demand and a positive integer work bound. It accepts no request, recipe, route, operation key, consumer key, target seat, desired result or success flag.

The existing IntegratedDemandController forms the exact route-free native request from current paid owned need evidence. The existing IntegratedRoutePolicy inventories alternatives, records reasons and selects the first eligible retained, ordinary, n, cp, consenting-support or defer option under its frozen priority policy.

No demand settles on selection or traversal alone. After a completed paid traversal, the controller deterministically derives one non-main native use operation from the realized movement destination and the exact movement output, pays it through ContentBridge, and calls the accepted settlement gate.

The derived consumer preserves actor, context, cue and semantic target. It consumes the exact traversal output and has a deterministic key beneath the formed request. It cannot introduce a new route, target or free completion.

A deferred, rejected, failed, cancelled, partial or unaffordable attempt remains visible and pending. The controller neither clears pressure nor fabricates an outcome. Repeated terminal steps are idempotent.
Conflicting demands retain the owned admission and first-seen order. A later demand cannot displace an earlier current paid owned demand by evaluator preference.
Checkpoint restoration is paired to the exact native engine state and restores the demand controller, route policy, phase, request, demand and event history. Continuation must be byte-identical.

TIM, seat dimensionality, native resource defaults, accepted subordinate policies and inherited source remain unchanged. Route traversal records dimensionality_changed=false and settlement grants no closure or capability certificate.

An independent auditor imports no autonomous-cycle controller. It invokes the accepted fulfillment and route-policy auditors and reconstructs the phase order, demand/request/traversal/consumer/settlement links, paid outputs, scope and exact paired checkpoint from raw records.

Acceptance requires the twelve exact new methods plus all 83 exact FT4.1/FT4.2 predecessor methods, both-setting raw witnesses, strict source freeze and unchanged source. Passing accepts FT4.3a only; FT4.3b still owes honest closure, later retained-capability reuse, unavailable support, opposition integration and the parent/common gate.
gate: Ninety-five exact methods pass with zero failures/errors; canonical and workflow witnesses originate in current owned demand, choose without route input, complete paid native traversal and deterministic paid consumption, settle only after actual consumption, pass independent reconstruction, match the registered source freeze and leave source unchanged.
next: FT4.3b honest closure, retained-capability-altered later choice, unavailable support, conflicting demand and opposition controls under the common FT4 gate
stop: Preserve failures; two gate failures after correction stops.
